abort.cannot_connect: Failed to connect. The charger accepts one Bluetooth client at a time, so close the phone app and try again.
abort.no_devices_found: No Spin EV charger was found over Bluetooth. Check that the charger is powered on, that no phone app is connected to it, and that Home Assistant has a Bluetooth adapter or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy in range of the charger.
abort.not_loaded: The charger must be set up and working before its connection can be changed.
abort.not_supported: This Bluetooth device is not a Spin EV charger.
abort.ocpp_port_in_use: Home Assistant could not start its OCPP central system, most likely because another program is using TCP port 9321.

user.description: How should Home Assistant reach the charger?

menu_options.ocpp: Over OCPP, for a charger already pointed at Home Assistant

data_description.address: The chargers discovered over Bluetooth, listed by serial number.

transport.description: Home Assistant can keep using Bluetooth, or point {name} at its own OCPP central system so it is reached over WiFi instead. OCPP has no range limit, leaves Bluetooth free for the phone app, and reports changes as they happen. The charger then stops using the vendor cloud. You can also stay on Bluetooth now and move to OCPP later, from Reconfigure.

bluetooth_to_ocpp.title: Point the charger at Home Assistant
bluetooth_to_ocpp.description:
{name} now connects to `{current}`. It will connect to Home Assistant on port {port} instead, and restart to apply the change.

If Home Assistant runs in a Docker container without host networking, the detected address is the container's own and the charger cannot reach it: enter the address of the machine running Docker instead, and publish port {port} from the container.

data_description.host: The IP address or host name the charger uses to reach Home Assistant. The detected address is filled in; change it only if the charger is on a different network.

menu_options.reconfigure_ocpp: Change the Home Assistant address the charger connects to

reconfigure_bluetooth.description: Home Assistant will reach the charger over Bluetooth again. The charger keeps its OCPP settings, so it can be moved back later; until then it works on its own and keeps its sessions to report later.

ocpp_timeout.description: {name} did not connect to Home Assistant in time. It may still be restarting, or the address may not be reachable from its network. You can set it up over Bluetooth now, and move it to OCPP later from Reconfigure. Continuing over Bluetooth gives the charger back its previous OCPP settings, which restarts it again.

menu_options.ocpp_finish: Use OCPP anyway, and wait for it in the background

ocpp_restore_failed.description: Home Assistant could not give {name} back its previous OCPP settings over Bluetooth. If you continue anyway, the charger keeps trying to reach Home Assistant over OCPP, and stays off the vendor cloud.

ocpp_port_in_use.description: Home Assistant could not start its OCPP central system, most likely because another program is using TCP port {port}. You can set it up over Bluetooth now, and move it to OCPP later from Reconfigure.

ocpp_read_failed.description: Home Assistant could not read the OCPP settings of {name} over Bluetooth. You can set it up over Bluetooth now, and move it to OCPP later from Reconfigure.

ocpp_write_failed.description: Home Assistant could not change the OCPP settings of {name} over Bluetooth. You can set it up over Bluetooth now, and move it to OCPP later from Reconfigure.

ocpp.description:
Point the charger's OCPP server at host `{host}`, port `{port}` and path `{path}`, keeping its charge point id.

If Home Assistant runs in a Docker container without host networking, the address above is the container's own and the charger cannot reach it: use the address of the machine running Docker instead, and publish port {port} from the container.

Once it has restarted and connected, select Submit.

data_description.charge_point_id: The chargers connected to Home Assistant, by charge point id.

ocpp_discovery_confirm.description: Charger {name} has connected to Home Assistant over OCPP. Do you want to set it up?

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the charger over Bluetooth. Close the phone app and try again.
error.invalid_host: Enter the address of this Home Assistant.
error.no_charger_connected: No new charger has connected yet. Check the address on the charger, wait for it to restart, then try again.

progress.ocpp_wait: Waiting for {name} to restart and connect to Home Assistant. This usually takes about half a minute.

cannot_write.message: Could not write to the charger: {error}

charger_booting.message: The charger is still starting up and will not accept commands yet.

charger_busy.message: The charger will not change its current limit during a session. Stop charging first, then try again.

command_rejected.message: The charger refused the command. The Bluetooth password is probably wrong.

device_not_found.message: Could not find the charger with address {address}. {reason}

no_vehicle_connected.message: No vehicle is connected, so charging cannot be started.

ocpp_not_connected.message: The charger with charge point id {charge_point_id} is not connected to Home Assistant over OCPP.

ocpp_port_in_use.message: Could not start the OCPP central system on port {port}: {error}

data_description.connection_mode: Stay connected holds the single Bluetooth slot for Home Assistant, so nobody else in range can pair with the charger, and it polls faster and fails less often. Reconnect each poll gives the slot up between polls so the phone app stays usable, at the cost of about a second of extra latency per poll and more reconnect churn.

init.description: The charger accepts one Bluetooth client at a time, so Home Assistant and the phone app cannot both be connected.
init.title: Connection
